name: Visitor Entry (ED Card)

requirements.blocker_text: Passport must not be more than 10 years old and must remain valid for the whole stay.
A completed and approved Embarkation and Disembarkation (ED) card is mandatory for entry.
Must prove ability to return to the country of departure or transit through another country.

evidence_required.document: Passport (under 10 years old, valid for whole stay)

outcome.duration_length: 30 days standard (US nationals up to 90 days); extensions up to 180 days per calendar year possible with a local guarantor or property ownership

sources.title: Aruba Tourism Authority (aruba.com) -- Immigration Regulations: passport, ED card, visa-exempt nationalities, 30/90/180-day stay rules, return-ticket requirement (used because no equivalent gov.aw/DIMAS visitor-entry page was located in this pass -- see notes)

notes: STATUS: DRAFT (tier-3 sourcing on every hard requirement -- no DIMAS/gov.aw visitor-entry page located; see below). NEW COUNTRY, first route of Aruba's initial build. Aruba is an autonomous constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands (ISO AW), like Curacao built earlier this session -- NOT a British Overseas Territory. Citizenship here is Dutch nationality via the Kingdom-level IND, not a local citizenship regime; see aw_naturalisation.json. Sourced to the Aruba Tourism Authority (ATA)'s own site rather than a DIMAS (immigration department) page, since no dedicated gov.aw/dimasaruba.aw visitor-entry/visa-policy page was surfaced in this pass -- ATA is Aruba's statutory tourism promotion authority, treated as tier 3 per this dataset's convention (not a tier-1 immigration authority, but an official government body with a direct operational role in entry logistics). Flagged as a gap to re-verify against a DIMAS-published entry-requirements page if one exists. No visa-required nationality list was retrieved -- modelled generally; citizens of the Netherlands, the US, and countries on the Netherlands' Schengen-linked visa-exempt list do not require a visa per this source.
